entries.new: visa on arrival, 30 days for the 17 the official list names; embassy visa for the 11 it does not
entries.note: The only official page we can read publishes one list and one allowance — 'may be issued a 30 day visitor visa on arrival' — and says citizens of all other countries need a visa before arrival. Publishing 90 days visa-free contradicted our own cited source. The eleven nationalities the list does not name are settled on the side that cannot mislead: a traveller who arranges a visa they did not need loses a fee, one who flies expecting entry loses the trip.

entries.reason: The business e-visa was cited to the tourist notice, which states a 28-day stay — the tourist visa's, not this one's. It now cites the business notice, which is the authority's own page for this visa and does not print the stay length, so it carries the official-portal mark.

entries.note: The official page states the visa is issued for 30, 60 or 90 days depending on the itinerary; we published the shortest of the three as though it were the only one.

entries.field: National (type D) visa fee — long stay, student, digital nomad, work
entries.note: Orden AUC/891/2024 raised the national long-stay visa fee to 90 euros, equalising it with the EU uniform visa fee after the Visa Code increase of June 2024. Our figure was the previous order's.

entries.reason: The 6,300 NOK figure is stated in the immigration regulation itself — § 17-10 first paragraph (a), "kr 6 300 i saker om arbeid eller studier" — rather than only on UDI's front page.

entries.field: National (type D) visa fee — residency, D7, D8, student, work
entries.note: Portaria n.º 91/2025/1 raised the national visa fee to 110 euros in March 2025; its own preamble notes the 90-euro figure had stood since 2011. Ours was the 2011 figure.

entries.field: Hong Kong, Serbia, South Korea, Türkiye — visa-free rows
entries.new: visa-free, with the portal's silence stated in the note
entries.note: The Immigration Agency's e-visa portal publishes a visa-free list of 60 nationalities that names Macau but not Hong Kong, and none of Serbia, South Korea or Türkiye, each of which we record under a bilateral arrangement. The portal's other column does not render for any reader we have, so we cannot tell absence from omission — the rows stand and the reader is told what the official list says.
